name: Dumbbell floor press
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, dumbbells over your chest.
Lower until your upper arms touch the floor, then pause.
Press straight up and squeeze your chest at the top.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the elbows off the floor
safety: Lay the dumbbells down at your sides, don't drop them over your face.
notes: Great no-bench option; the shorter range is kind to cranky shoulders.

name: Dumbbell floor fly
form_cues: Lie on the floor with a soft bend in your elbows.
Open your arms wide until elbows lightly touch the floor.
Hug the weights back up over your chest.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows into a press
safety: Use light weights and keep the elbow bend fixed.
notes: The floor stops the stretch, so it is safer than a bench fly for beginners.

name: Standing dumbbell shoulder press
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward.
Squeeze glutes and abs, then press straight overhead.
Lower with control back to your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to finish the rep
Pressing the weights forward instead of up
safety: Keep your ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch.

name: Arnold press
form_cues: Start with dumbbells at chin height, palms facing you.
Rotate palms forward as you press overhead.
Reverse the turn on the way down.
safety: Go lighter than your normal press; the rotation loads the shoulder more.
notes: Usually done seated on an upright bench; standing works too.

name: Dumbbell lateral raise
form_cues: Stand tall with a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the weights out to the sides to shoulder height.
Lower slowly over two to three seconds.
safety: Stop at shoulder height if you get any pinching.

name: Leaning single-arm lateral raise
form_cues: Hold a post and lean away with your arm straight.
Raise the dumbbell out to the side to shoulder height.
Lower slowly and keep the lean steady.
common_mistakes: Turning it into an upright row
safety: Hold something solid that will not move when you lean on it.
notes: The lean keeps tension on the side delt at the bottom of the rep.

name: Dumbbell front raise
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms down.
Raise to eye level with straight but soft arms.
Lower slowly without swinging back.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to lift the weight
safety: Keep it light; front delts already get lots of work from pressing.
notes: Alternate arms or use a neutral grip if your shoulders feel pinchy.

name: Bent-over dumbbell reverse fly
form_cues: Hinge forward until your chest is nearly parallel to the floor.
With soft elbows, raise the weights out wide.
Pause, then lower without letting your torso bob.
common_mistakes: Using the back to swing the weights
Squeezing the shoulder blades instead of moving the arms
safety: Keep a flat back and brace; sit down on a bench if your lower back tires.

name: Dumbbell upright row
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Lead with your elbows and lift to lower-chest height.
Lower under control.
common_mistakes: Shrugging instead of lifting with the elbows
safety: Stop below shoulder height if you feel a pinch in the front of the shoulder.
notes: Dumbbells let your hands move freely, which is easier on the wrists than a bar.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead press
form_cues: Stand tall with one dumbbell at your shoulder.
Brace your abs and press straight up without leaning.
Lower slowly back to the shoulder.
safety: Keep the free hand on your belly to feel your abs stay tight.

name: Half-kneeling single-arm dumbbell press
form_cues: Kneel with the same-side knee down as the pressing arm.
Squeeze the down-side glute and stay tall.
Press up slightly in front of your head, then lower.
safety: Pad the down knee with a mat or folded towel.
notes: The kneeling stance stops you cheating with the lower back.

name: Dumbbell Z press
form_cues: Sit on the floor with legs straight out in front.
Sit tall without leaning back, dumbbells at shoulders.
Press overhead and lower with control.
safety: If tight hamstrings round your back, bend your knees slightly or sit on a plate.
notes: Named after strongman Zydrunas Savickas; exposes weak core and mobility.

name: Dumbbell push press
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders, feet hip-width.
Dip a few inches at the knees, then drive up hard.
Use the leg drive to press overhead; lower with control.
common_mistakes: Dipping too deep like a squat
safety: Keep the dip short and the knees tracking over your toes.
notes: Lets you handle more weight overhead than a strict press.

name: Dumbbell Cuban press
form_cues: Upright-row light dumbbells until elbows reach shoulder height.
Rotate forearms up so your hands are over your elbows.
Press overhead, then reverse each step.
safety: Use very light weights; this is a shoulder-health drill, not a strength test.

name: Side-lying dumbbell external rotation
form_cues: Lie on your side, top elbow bent 90° and pinned to your ribs.
Rotate the forearm up toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly without the elbow lifting off your side.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbow leave the body
safety: Start with 1–3 kg; stop if you feel sharp pain.
notes: A rolled towel under the elbow helps keep good position.

name: Dumbbell Lu raise
form_cues: Hold light dumbbells at your sides, thumbs up.
Raise straight-armed out to the side and keep going overhead.
Lower slowly along the same path.
safety: Only take it overhead if you can do so without pain.
notes: Named after Olympic lifter Lu Xiaojun; works the top range of the shoulder.

name: Dumbbell scaption raise
form_cues: Stand with thumbs pointing up.
Raise arms in a Y shape, about 30° in front of your sides.
Stop at shoulder height and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Lifting straight out to the side
safety: Keep it light and pain-free.
notes: Often used in shoulder rehab; the angle matches how the shoulder blade sits.

name: Dumbbell high pull
form_cues: Hold dumbbells in front of your thighs, hinge slightly.
Drive your hips forward explosively.
Let the pop carry the weights up, elbows high and out.
safety: Keep the weights close to your body and your back flat.

name: Bent-over dumbbell row
form_cues: Hinge forward with a flat back, weights hanging under your shoulders.
Row elbows back toward your hips.
Squeeze at the top, then lower all the way.
safety: Brace your abs; if your lower back fatigues, switch to a supported row.

name: Dumbbell gorilla row
form_cues: Stand wide, hinge forward, dumbbells on the floor between your feet.
Row one weight up while the other arm pushes into its dumbbell.
Lower and alternate sides.
safety: Keep your hips level and back flat throughout.
notes: Popular with kettlebells; dumbbells work just as well.

name: Dumbbell rear delt row
form_cues: Hinge forward with palms facing your legs or behind you.
Row with elbows flared out wide, about 70–90°.
Pull until upper arms line up with your torso.
common_mistakes: Pulling elbows to the hips like a lat row
safety: Keep a neutral spine and brace your core.

name: Dumbbell shrug
form_cues: Stand tall with heavy dumbbells at your sides.
Shrug your shoulders straight up toward your ears.
Hold one second, then lower fully.
safety: Keep your neck neutral; don't jut your chin forward.
notes: Use straps if grip gives out before your traps.

name: Dumbbell deadlift
form_cues: Stand with dumbbells at your sides or in front of your shins.
Push hips back and bend knees until weights reach mid-shin.
Stand up by driving through your feet and squeezing your glutes.
common_mistakes: Letting the weights drift away from your legs
safety: Keep your spine neutral and brace before every rep.

name: Dumbbell suitcase deadlift
form_cues: Stand with one dumbbell at your side.
Hinge and bend knees to lower it beside your foot.
Stand up without leaning toward the weight.
common_mistakes: Tilting the shoulders toward the dumbbell
safety: Stay square and stop if you can't keep your torso upright.
notes: Doubles as anti-lateral-flexion core training.

name: Dumbbell Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand tall, soft knees, dumbbells in front of your thighs.
Push your hips back and slide the weights down your legs.
Stop at a deep hamstring stretch, then drive hips forward.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back to go lower
safety: Only go as low as you can with a flat back.
notes: Strict stiff-leg version: knees nearly straight and weights to the floor.

name: Dumbbell B-stance Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Put most weight on the front leg, back toes lightly down beside its heel.
Hinge hips back with a flat back.
Drive through the front heel to stand tall.
safety: Keep the back foot as a kickstand for balance only.
notes: Bridge between two-leg and single-leg RDLs.

name: Single-leg Romanian deadlift
form_cues: Stand on one leg with a soft knee, weight in the opposite hand.
Hinge forward as your free leg reaches straight back.
Keep hips square and return to standing.
common_mistakes: Opening the hip toward the ceiling
safety: Use a wall or rack with your free hand if balance is shaky.

name: Dumbbell curl
form_cues: Stand tall, elbows tucked at your sides, palms forward.
Curl up and squeeze at the top.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
safety: Keep wrists neutral; drop the weight if you have to swing it.
notes: Curl both arms together or alternate them.

name: Hammer curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing each other.
Curl up keeping thumbs on top.
Lower under control to full extension.
safety: Keep elbows pinned to your sides.

name: Cross-body hammer curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with thumbs up.
Curl one weight across your body toward the opposite shoulder.
Lower slowly and alternate.
safety: Keep the shoulder still; only the forearm moves.

name: Zottman curl
form_cues: Curl up with palms facing up.
At the top, turn palms down.
Lower slowly with palms down, then turn back at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Using a weight too heavy for the palms-down part
safety: Pick a weight you can control on the way down.
notes: Trains biceps up and forearms on the way down.

name: Dumbbell reverse curl
form_cues: Hold dumbbells with palms facing down.
Curl up keeping wrists straight.
Lower slowly.
safety: Go light; the overhand grip limits the load.

name: Concentration curl
form_cues: Sit with your elbow braced on your inner thigh.
Curl the weight toward your shoulder.
Squeeze, then lower to full extension.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the thigh
safety: Use a stable seat; any bench or chair works.

name: Dumbbell waiter curl
form_cues: Cup one end of a dumbbell in both palms, like a tray.
Curl it up keeping elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly without the dumbbell tipping.
safety: Hold the dumbbell securely so it can't slip out.
notes: Keeps the biceps under tension at the top.

name: Overhead dumbbell extension
form_cues: Hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands under the top plate.
Lower it behind your head, elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms fully at the top.
safety: Sit down with back support if your lower back arches.

name: Single-arm overhead dumbbell extension
form_cues: Hold a dumbbell overhead, arm straight.
Lower it behind your head, elbow pointing up.
Extend back up; support the elbow with your free hand if needed.
safety: Lower slowly to protect the elbow.

name: Dumbbell triceps kickback
form_cues: Hinge forward and pin upper arms by your sides.
Straighten your elbows to push the weights back.
Pause at full lockout, then lower slowly.
safety: Keep your back flat; support one hand on a bench if needed.
notes: Can be done one arm at a time with a hand on a bench.

name: Wrist curl
form_cues: Rest forearms on your thighs or a bench, palms up, wrists off the edge.
Let the dumbbells roll down toward your fingers.
Curl your wrists up as high as you can.
safety: Use light weights and smooth reps.

name: Reverse wrist curl
form_cues: Rest forearms on your thighs, palms down, wrists off the edge.
Lift the backs of your hands toward the ceiling.
Lower slowly.
safety: Very light weights are enough; this can help with tennis elbow rehab.

name: Dumbbell pronation and supination
form_cues: Rest your forearm on your thigh, hold one end of a dumbbell.
Slowly rotate palm up, then palm down.
Keep the forearm still the whole time.
common_mistakes: Using a weight that's too heavy
safety: Holding further from the end makes it harder; start close.
notes: A hammer works if you don't have a light dumbbell.

name: Farmer's carry
form_cues: Pick up heavy dumbbells with a flat back.
Stand tall, shoulders down, and walk with short steps.
Set them down with control at the end.
safety: Clear your path and deadlift the weights down, don't drop them.
notes: Track the weight per hand; distance or time goes in the reps.

name: Dumbbell pinch hold
form_cues: Grab a hex dumbbell by one end with fingers and thumb only.
Stand and hold it at your side.
Squeeze hard until time is up.
safety: Hold it beside your foot, not over it, in case it slips.
notes: Pinching two plates together is a common alternative.

name: Goblet squat
form_cues: Hold one dumbbell vertically against your chest.
Sit down between your knees, chest tall.
Drive up through your whole foot.
safety: Keep your heels down; stop if your knees hurt.

name: Dumbbell squat
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides, feet shoulder-width.
Squat down keeping your chest up and knees over toes.
Stand by pushing the floor away.
safety: Keep the weights hanging straight; don't let them hit your knees.

name: Dumbbell front squat
form_cues: Rest one end of each dumbbell on your shoulders, elbows high.
Squat down keeping your torso upright.
Drive up without letting the elbows drop.
safety: Brace hard; the weight sits on your shoulders, so keep a tight upper back.

name: Heels-elevated dumbbell squat
form_cues: Put your heels on a wedge or small plate, feet close.
Hold dumbbells at your sides or one at your chest.
Sink straight down letting knees travel forward.
safety: Make sure the heel support can't slide out.
notes: Raised heels shift work to the quads; a weight plate is a handy wedge.

name: Dumbbell sumo squat
form_cues: Stand wide, toes turned out, one dumbbell hanging between your legs.
Push knees out and sit straight down.
Squeeze your glutes to stand up.
safety: Stand on two plates or steps if you want the dumbbell to go deeper.

name: Dumbbell cossack squat
form_cues: Stand very wide holding a dumbbell at your chest.
Sit down over one leg while the other stays straight, toes up.
Push back to the middle and switch sides.
common_mistakes: Heel of the bent leg lifting
safety: Only go as deep as your hips allow without pain.
notes: Great for adductor strength and hip mobility.

name: Dumbbell split squat
form_cues: Stand in a long split stance with dumbbells at your sides.
Lower your back knee straight down toward the floor.
Drive through the front foot to come up; finish all reps then switch.
safety: Pad the floor under your back knee if it touches.

name: Dumbbell forward lunge
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides.
Step forward and lower until both knees bend about 90°.
Push off the front foot back to standing.
safety: Step far enough that your front heel stays down.

name: Dumbbell reverse lunge
form_cues: Stand tall, dumbbells at your sides.
Step back and lower your back knee toward the floor.
Drive through the front heel to return.
safety: Easier on the knees than forward lunges.

name: Dumbbell deficit reverse lunge
form_cues: Stand on a low step holding dumbbells.
Step back off it and sink deep.
Drive through the front foot to step back up.
safety: Use a stable step no higher than about 10 cm.
notes: The extra depth stretches the glutes more than a normal lunge.

name: Dumbbell walking lunge
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides and step forward into a lunge.
Lower the back knee close to the floor.
Drive forward into the next step without pausing upright.
safety: Make sure you have a clear path.

name: Dumbbell lateral lunge
form_cues: Hold a dumbbell at your chest.
Step wide to the side and sit back into that hip.
Keep the other leg straight, then push back to centre.
safety: Keep toes pointing forward or slightly out.

name: Dumbbell curtsy lunge
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides or one at your chest.
Step one leg diagonally behind the other, like a curtsy.
Lower, then drive through the front heel to return.
safety: Stop short of any knee discomfort; it's a twisting angle.

name: Dumbbell overhead walking lunge
form_cues: Press dumbbells overhead and lock your arms.
Walk forward in lunges keeping your arms vertical.
Keep ribs down and steps controlled.
safety: Use light weights; lower them with control if you lose position.
notes: Single-arm overhead version is a common CrossFit option.

name: Single-arm dumbbell overhead squat
form_cues: Press one dumbbell overhead and lock the arm.
Squat down keeping the arm vertical and eyes forward.
Stand up without the weight drifting.
safety: Practise with no weight first; it needs good shoulder mobility.

name: Dumbbell glute bridge
form_cues: Lie on your back, knees bent, dumbbell resting on your hip crease.
Drive through your heels and lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top, then lower.
common_mistakes: Arching the lower back at the top
safety: Hold the dumbbell with both hands and pad it with a towel.

name: Single-leg dumbbell glute bridge
form_cues: Lie down, one foot planted, other leg lifted, dumbbell on the working hip.
Push through the planted heel to raise your hips.
Keep the hips level as you lower.
safety: Hold the dumbbell steady with your hand so it can't roll.

name: Dumbbell frog pump
form_cues: Lie down, soles of the feet together, knees out wide.
Rest a dumbbell on your hips.
Drive your hips up fast and squeeze, then lower.
safety: Keep reps smooth; stop if your hips feel pinchy.
notes: A high-rep glute burnout.

name: Dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides, balls of feet on a step.
Lower heels for a deep stretch.
Rise as high as you can and pause.
safety: Hold a rail with one hand if balance is an issue.
notes: Works fine on flat floor if you have no step.

name: Single-leg dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Stand on one foot on a step, dumbbell in the same-side hand.
Lower the heel slowly below the step.
Push up as high as possible and pause.
common_mistakes: Using the free hand to pull up
safety: Lightly hold a wall for balance only.

name: Dumbbell tiptoe farmer's walk
form_cues: Pick up dumbbells and rise onto the balls of your feet.
Walk with short steps without letting heels touch.
Stay tall and set the weights down with control.
safety: Use moderate weights; rolling an ankle is the main risk.

name: Bent-over dumbbell trap-3 raise
form_cues: Hinge forward, one hand on a bench or thigh.
Raise a light dumbbell up and out at about 45°, thumb up.
Pull the shoulder blade down and back; lower slowly.
safety: Use 1–4 kg; it's a small muscle.
notes: Helps posture and shoulder blade control.

name: Dumbbell thruster
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your shoulders and squat down.
Drive up hard and use the momentum to press overhead.
Lower to the shoulders as you sink into the next squat.
safety: Keep your core braced and don't arch at the top.

name: Single-arm dumbbell snatch
form_cues: Start with the dumbbell between your feet, hips back, flat back.
Explode up through the hips and pull the dumbbell high and close.
Punch it overhead and stand tall; lower in stages.
common_mistakes: Pressing it up instead of pulling
Rounding the back at the start
safety: Learn it light; lower the weight to the shoulder first, then the floor.
notes: Alternate arms each rep for conditioning work.

name: Dumbbell hang clean
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at mid-thigh with a flat back.
Jump the hips forward and shrug the weights up.
Drop under and catch them on your shoulders, knees soft.
safety: Keep the dumbbells close to your body on the way up.

name: Dumbbell squat clean
form_cues: Start with dumbbells on the floor beside your feet.
Pull explosively and drop into a front squat to catch them.
Stand up tall with the weights on your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back off the floor
safety: Brace before every pull and keep a flat back.

name: Dumbbell clean and press
form_cues: Hang-clean the dumbbells to your shoulders.
Re-set your feet and brace.
Press or push-press overhead, then lower to the thighs.
common_mistakes: Rushing the press before you're stable
safety: Lower the weights in two steps to protect your back.

name: Dumbbell cluster
form_cues: Clean the dumbbells from the floor into a front squat.
Drive straight up out of the squat.
Use the momentum to press overhead in one motion.
safety: Very demanding; scale weight and reps to keep form crisp.
notes: A CrossFit staple: a squat clean flowing into a thruster.

name: Renegade row
form_cues: Get into a push-up position holding hex dumbbells, feet wide.
Row one dumbbell to your hip without twisting.
Set it down softly and alternate.
safety: Use hex dumbbells so they can't roll and catch your wrists.
notes: Add a push-up between rows for a harder version.

name: Devil press
form_cues: Do a burpee with your hands on the dumbbells.
Jump the feet in and swing both weights back between your legs.
Snap the hips to swing them straight overhead in one motion.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back on the swing
safety: Start light; the swing should come from the hips, not the lower back.

name: Man maker
form_cues: Push-up on the dumbbells, then row each side once.
Jump the feet in and clean the weights to your shoulders.
Squat and press overhead (thruster); that's one rep.
common_mistakes: Rushing the clean with a round back
safety: Use hex dumbbells and a modest weight; form fades fast as you tire.

name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift high pull
form_cues: Stand wide holding one dumbbell by the head with both hands.
Drive through your legs and hips explosively.
Pull the dumbbell to chin height, elbows high, then lower.
safety: Keep the dumbbell close and stop the pull below your chin.

name: Dumbbell sumo deadlift
form_cues: Stand wide, toes out, one dumbbell on end between your feet.
Sit hips back and grab the handle with a flat back.
Push the floor apart to stand up, squeezing glutes.
safety: Stand on two plates if the dumbbell is too low to reach with a flat back.

name: Seated dumbbell shoulder press
form_cues: Set the bench upright and sit with your back flat on the pad.
Start with dumbbells at ear height, elbows slightly forward.
Press up until arms are straight, then lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Cutting the range short at the bottom
safety: Kick the dumbbells up off your knees one at a time to get into position.
notes: A flat bench works too; sitting without back support adds core work.

name: Flat dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie back with feet flat and shoulder blades pinched together.
Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your chest, elbows about 45°.
Press up and slightly in until arms are straight.
common_mistakes: Clanking the weights at the top
safety: Kick the dumbbells up from your knees and lower them back to your knees when done.

name: Neutral-grip dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie on a flat bench, palms facing each other.
Lower with elbows close to your sides.
Press straight up, keeping the dumbbells parallel.
safety: A shoulder-friendly option if regular pressing aches.
notes: More triceps than the standard grip.

name: Single-arm dumbbell bench press
form_cues: Lie on a bench with one dumbbell, other hand on your belly.
Lower it to your chest without twisting.
Press up while keeping your hips and shoulders flat.
safety: Start light; the unevenness takes getting used to.
notes: Doubles as anti-rotation core work.

name: Dumbbell squeeze press
form_cues: Lie on a bench and press the dumbbells together over your chest.
Keep squeezing them together as you lower to your chest.
Press back up without letting them separate.
safety: Hex dumbbells are easiest to squeeze; keep wrists straight.

name: Incline dumbbell press
form_cues: Set the bench to about 30°, not steeper.
Lower to the upper chest with elbows slightly tucked.
Press up and slightly in, without clanking the dumbbells.
safety: Lower until you feel a chest stretch, never pain in the shoulder.

name: Decline dumbbell press
form_cues: Hook your feet under the pads and lie back.
Lower the dumbbells to your lower chest.
Press up and slightly in.
common_mistakes: Letting the weights drift over your face
safety: Have a partner hand you the dumbbells, or start with them on your thighs.
notes: Some adjustable benches decline; otherwise use a fixed decline bench.

name: Dumbbell fly
form_cues: Soft bend in the elbows, locked in.
Open wide until you feel a chest stretch.
Hug the weights back up over your chest.
safety: Go light; this is a stretch move.

name: Incline dumbbell fly
form_cues: Set the bench to 30° and hold dumbbells over your upper chest.
Open your arms wide with a fixed elbow bend.
Squeeze them back together over your chest.
safety: Keep the weight light enough to control the stretch.

name: Decline dumbbell fly
form_cues: Secure your feet and lie back on a decline bench.
Open arms wide with soft elbows.
Bring the weights back together over your lower chest.
safety: Sit up carefully at the end with the weights held close to your chest.

name: Dumbbell pullover
form_cues: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest with both hands.
With slightly bent elbows, lower it back behind your head.
Pull it back over your chest using chest and lats.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows like a triceps extension
safety: Grip the dumbbell securely and stop before your shoulders feel strained.
notes: Lying across the bench is the classic old-school version.

name: One-arm dumbbell row
form_cues: Knee and hand on the bench, back flat.
Pull the dumbbell toward your hip, not your armpit.
Lower until your arm is fully straight.
safety: Keep your neck neutral and your back flat.

name: Kroc row
form_cues: Brace one hand on a bench, feet staggered.
Row a heavy dumbbell for high reps with a little body English.
Lower to a full stretch each rep.
common_mistakes: Turning it into a full-body jerk
safety: Use straps if needed and keep the lower back neutral.
notes: Named after powerlifter Matt Kroczaleski.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell row
form_cues: Lie face down on a bench set to 30–45°.
Let the dumbbells hang, then row elbows toward your hips.
Squeeze your shoulder blades and lower slowly.
common_mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad
safety: A great option when your lower back is tired.

name: Chest-supported dumbbell reverse fly
form_cues: Lie face down on an incline bench.
With soft elbows, raise the dumbbells out wide.
Pause at the top, then lower under control.
common_mistakes: Squeezing shoulder blades instead of moving the arms
safety: Use light weights; rear delts are small.

name: Incline dumbbell Y raise
form_cues: Lie face down on a 30–45° incline, thumbs up.
Raise the dumbbells in a Y shape in line with your ears.
Lower slowly without shrugging.
safety: Use very light dumbbells (1–5 kg).
notes: Good for posture and shoulder blade control.

name: Incline dumbbell shrug
form_cues: Lie face down on an incline bench, arms hanging.
Shrug your shoulders up and back toward each other.
Hold briefly, then lower.
safety: Keep your chest on the pad.
notes: Targets the middle traps more than standing shrugs.

name: Lying side lateral raise
form_cues: Lie on your side on an incline bench.
Raise the top arm out until it points up.
Lower slowly to below the bench line.
safety: Use a light weight; keep it pain-free.
notes: Loads the bottom of the lateral raise that standing raises miss.

name: Incline dumbbell curl
form_cues: Sit back on a 45–60° bench, arms hanging straight down.
Curl up without moving your elbows forward.
Lower all the way to a full stretch.
common_mistakes: Lifting the head and shoulders off the pad
safety: Go lighter than normal curls; the stretch is demanding.

name: Incline hammer curl
form_cues: Sit back on an incline bench, palms facing in.
Curl up with thumbs leading.
Lower slowly to full stretch.
safety: Keep shoulders back on the pad.

name: Dumbbell spider curl
form_cues: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, arms hanging.
Curl up and squeeze hard at the top.
Lower slowly without swinging.
common_mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad
safety: Keep your chin over the top of the bench, not resting on it.

name: Dumbbell preacher curl
form_cues: Rest the back of your upper arm on the pad.
Curl the dumbbell up and squeeze.
Lower slowly but stop just short of locking out hard.
common_mistakes: Lifting the elbow off the pad
safety: Control the bottom to protect the elbow.
notes: No preacher bench? Lean over the back of an incline bench.

name: Dumbbell skull crusher
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells over your shoulders, palms facing each other.
Bend the elbows to lower the weights beside your head.
Straighten your arms, keeping upper arms still.
safety: Lower slowly; the weights end up near your head.

name: Tate press
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells over your chest, palms toward your feet.
Bend the elbows out to lower the dumbbell ends to your chest.
Extend back up by squeezing your triceps.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows drop toward your sides
safety: Use light weights and lower with control.

name: Close-grip dumbbell press
form_cues: Lie on a bench, dumbbells touching, palms facing each other.
Lower them to your lower chest with elbows tucked.
Press straight up with the weights still touching.
safety: Keep the weights over your chest, not your face.

name: Lying cross-body triceps extension
form_cues: Lie on a bench with one dumbbell straight up.
Bend the elbow so the weight lowers toward the opposite shoulder.
Extend back up.
safety: Lower slowly so the dumbbell doesn't hit your chest.

name: Bulgarian split squat
form_cues: Rest your back foot laces-down on a bench.
Lower straight down until the front thigh is near parallel.
Drive through the front heel to stand.
common_mistakes: Front foot too close to the bench
safety: Find your stance with no weight first; stop if the knee hurts.
notes: Lean forward slightly for more glute, stay upright for more quad.

name: Front-foot elevated split squat
form_cues: Put your front foot on a low step, back foot on the floor.
Sink until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive up through the front foot.
safety: Use a stable step about 5–10 cm high.
notes: Gives more depth than a regular split squat.

name: Dumbbell step-up
form_cues: Place your whole foot on a knee-height box or bench.
Drive through that heel to stand up tall.
Step down slowly with the same leg leading back.
safety: Make sure the bench or box is solid and won't tip.

name: Dumbbell lateral step-up
form_cues: Stand side-on to a box with dumbbells at your sides.
Step the near foot up and stand tall.
Lower slowly back down on the same side.
safety: Use a lower box to start.

name: Dumbbell box step-over
form_cues: Hold dumbbells at your sides facing a box.
Step up, stand tall on top, and step down the other side.
Turn and repeat, alternating legs.
safety: Step, don't jump, down from the box with weights in hand.
notes: Common in CrossFit workouts; count total reps.

name: Dumbbell hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench edge, dumbbell on your hips.
Drive through your heels and raise hips to a straight line.
Tuck your chin and squeeze glutes hard at the top.
safety: Pad the dumbbell and hold it in place with both hands.

name: Single-leg dumbbell hip thrust
form_cues: Upper back on a bench, dumbbell on the working hip.
Lift one foot and drive through the other heel.
Keep hips level and lower slowly.
safety: Start with bodyweight to master the balance.

name: Dumbbell lying leg curl
form_cues: Lie face down with knees just off the bench end.
Squeeze a dumbbell between your feet.
Curl heels toward your glutes and lower slowly.
safety: Have a partner place the dumbbell, and keep it light.
notes: A home substitute for the leg curl machine.

name: Seated dumbbell calf raise
form_cues: Sit with balls of the feet on a plate or step.
Rest dumbbells on your knees.
Lower heels, then press up as high as possible.
safety: Pad the dumbbells on your knees with a towel.
